north.title: Israeli Enemy Steps Up Attacks on Southern Lebanon
north.text: Israeli occupation forces escalated their attacks across southern Lebanon from midnight Saturday into Sunday, Al-Manar reporters across southern Lebanon reported Sunday, in a continued series of daily violations of Lebanese territory. The occupation army carried out airstrikes, artillery shelling and machine-gun fire while moving military vehicles through several towns, our correspondents reported. Israeli warplanes launched two airstrikes on Al-Mansouri and separate strikes on Tallousa and Kfar Tebnit. Al-Manar correspondent in southern Lebanon reports two Israeli strikes on Al-Mansouri in Tyre district. — Al-Manar English (@manarenglish) October 11, 2026 Meanwhile, Israeli artillery shelling targeted Slouqi, Hujair and Zibqin valleys, the outskirts of Shaqra, Houla and Qantara and Mansouri, as well as the outskirts of Zawtar Al-Sharqiya near Mayfadoun, according to Al-Manar reporters. An Israeli demolition operation was also reported in Byout Al-Seyyad. Israeli occupation forces directed machine-gun fire toward Barashit, Zawtar Al-Sharqiya, Beit Yahoun and Hadatha, as well as the area between Wadi Halta and the outskirts of Kfarshouba. The gunfire near Kfarshouba coincided with residents harvesting olives in the area, placing civilians pursuing seasonal agricultural work in risk amid the ongoing Israeli attacks. Israeli military vehicles also moved through Beit Yahoun, accompanied by machine-gun fire, while additional vehicle movements were reported in Kfar Tebnit. In Hadatha, Israeli vehicles moved through the town amid further machine-gun fire. The latest attacks come amid persistent Israeli violations across southern Lebanon, involving airstrikes, artillery shelling, gunfire and military movements in Lebanese territory on daily basis despite a ceasefire agreement.

Sarit Zehavi for The Jerusalem Post – Did the Pager Operation Change the Middle East? – Opinion
north.text: Hezbollah is weaker, but it’s not disappeared. It still possesses thousands of rockets and missiles and continues to invest in expanding its drone capabilities The unequivocal answer is yes. But the story is far more complex than a one-word answer. The operation had two main achievements. The first was psychological. It restored Israel’s standing as a security power capable of carrying out operations that had seemed unimaginable or impossible. After October 7, it demonstrated to the region in which we live that Israel had recovered and was capable of penetrating even its enemies’ most sensitive systems. This was enormously important for Israel’s deterrence. Hezbollah, the strongest and most important militia in the Shi’ite axis, suddenly found itself in deep distress and embarrassment. Read the analysis in The Jerusalem Post. north.title: Deadly attack on airport in Saudi Arabia's capital kills 12
north.text: Saudi Arabia on Sunday extended the closure of the country's main international airport , according to an online flight tracker, a day after a missile attack on the facility killed 12 people from several countries and left more than 300 injured in a major escalation of the war between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and the kingdom. A Saudi-led coalition blamed Saturday afternoon's attack on the Houthis. It was the latest of several in the past week at King Khalid International Airport in the capital, Riyadh, and marked the deadliest attack in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war. Saudi Arabia is the world's top oil exporter, and the attacks have sent up oil prices and rattled markets. Following the attack, US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was weighing whether the United States would join Saudi strikes against the rebels. Airport operations were suspended Saturday. Authorities later extended the closure until at least 9PM. Sunday, according to Flightradar24. Also on Sunday, the Houthi-run Health Ministry said 91 Yemenis were killed and 168 injured by the Saudi-led coalition in five weeks. It said 60 percent of those killed were women and children. Mix of nationalities killed at Saudi airport The attack struck an airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorised to speak to the media. The Saudi statement said the dead included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said several hospitals were treating the injured. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged in a social media post that an American citizen had been killed in the attack, which he condemned. north.title: Attack on Riyadh airport leaves 12 dead, more than 300 injured
north.text: Attack on Riyadh airport leaves 12 dead, more than 300 injured At least 12 people were killed and 309 others injured in an attack on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh as Yemen's Houthis escalated the campaign they launched this summer against the kingdom. The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said in a statement on Sunday that four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed in the attack late Saturday. The authority said some of the injured were in critical condition and that all were receiving medical care at several hospitals. Hospitals were flooded with wounded brought by ambulance and helicopter, people briefed on the matter told Reuters. Jordan's foreign ministry said in a statement on Saturday that two injured Jordanians were discharged from hospital while two others were still receiving treatment. ukraine.title: Authorities expand mandatory evacuation zone for children in Kramatorsk
ukraine.text: Donetsk Oblast Military Administration has decided to expand the zone where children must be evacuated from certain areas of Kramatorsk. Source: Vadym Filashkin, Head of Donetsk Oblast Military Administration, on Facebook Quote: "The evacuation will be carried out with parents, guardians or legal representatives accompanying the children. Local military administrations, the police, rescue workers and the children's services are involved in the operation." Details: Filashkin said the decision was made to prevent further child casualties. He promised that people would be accompanied at every stage, from departure to arrival at a reception centre and subsequent accommodation in safer regions. "The safety situation is deteriorating, and waiting until the danger reaches your home is too great a risk. This is especially true when children are involved. I urge parents not to delay. Evacuation saves lives," the head of the administration stressed. He also published a list of streets from which the evacuation will be carried out. Kramatorsk is just over 10 km from the front line. Background: On the morning of 8 October, Russian forces attacked Kramatorsk. The strike on two buses killed 30 people and injured 18 . Later, two people were killed when a Russian drone struck a car in Kramatorsk. This brought the death toll from Russian attacks in the city on 8 October to 32. On 8 October, three people were killed in the settlement of Bilenke, which borders Kramatorsk. Subscribe on Patreon to back our journalism long-term.

ukraine.title: European Commission will propose visa restrictions for Russians in January, Politico reports
ukraine.text: The European Commission is finalising plans to tighten visa rules for hundreds of thousands of Russians who visit EU countries as tourists every year, aiming to strengthen the EU's defences against hybrid attacks. Source: Politico , citing EU officials, as reported by European Pravda Details: The EU representatives said the European Commission plans to put forward the proposals in the new year after a group of countries, including Poland, Sweden and Estonia, pushed for stricter visa rules for Russians, including former combatants who fought against Ukraine. Last year, Russian citizens were issued around 478,000 Schengen tourist visas, a significant proportion of which were multiple-entry visas. Swedish Justice Minister Gunnar Strömmer believes this system poses a threat to European security amid growing concerns about acts of sabotage, arson and other forms of hybrid warfare sponsored by Moscow. " It's obvious I think for everyone that we have vulnerabilities in our system that can be used by our enemies. As far as I understand things, the Commission is preparing a proposal that, according to what I have heard, should be launched in January next year. From a Swedish point of view, we would love to see it even earlier ," Strömmer told Politico. Strömmer welcomed the " progress " and " growing support " for introducing a stricter visa regime for Russians. Other countries plan to raise the issue at the Foreign Affairs Council meeting on 12 October and propose additional restrictions on Russian diplomats in the EU. Estonia has proposed a complete ban on entry to the EU for former members of the Russian armed forces. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said there are around 650,000 of these former combatants , and they would be banned from entering " person by person ".

ukraine.title: Trump claims Putin "strongly" wants deal to end war
ukraine.text: US President Donald Trump has claimed that Russian ruler Vladimir Putin really wants to end his war against Ukraine. Source: Trump's comments to journalists on 10 October, as reported by European Pravda Details: Journalists asked Trump what Putin had told him during their phone conversation on 9 October. Quote: " He'd like to see a settlement. President Putin would like to see a settlement strongly. " [N.B. Ukrainska Pravda does not recognise Putin as president – ed.] Details: Trump then added that Russia supplies significant quantities of oil to the global market. " And look, he's freeing up a lot of oil for the world. Okay. A good thing. And by the way, at a very low price ," he said. Background: On 9 October, Trump said he had had a " highly successful discussion " with Putin and reached an agreement on lifting sanctions on Russian diesel fuel . The agreement between Trump and Putin sparked outrage in Ukraine and European capitals. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy strongly criticised Trump's actions , describing the easing of sanctions as an "absolutely terrible" move. Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal called the US president's decision a major mistake and urged increased support for Ukraine so that it could turn Russian oil refineries into ruins . The Finnish prime minister described the agreement as "a terrible disappointment" . EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Europe will not ease its pressure on Russia following the agreement between Trump and Putin. Subscribe on Patreon to back our journalism long-term.

ukraine.title: Court orders Russia to pay agricultural company US$2m for property seized in Zaporizhzhia Oblast
ukraine.text: The Commercial Court of Zaporizhzhia Oblast has ordered the Russian Federation to pay Agro Alliance LLC UAH 101.74 million (US$2.2 million) in damages and lost profits for property lost in temporarily occupied territory. Source: the court's ruling Details: Agro Alliance is registered in the village of Kopani, Zaporizhzhia Oblast. The company grew cereals, legumes and oilseeds and engaged in wholesale grain trading, among other activities. According to the case documents, in early March 2022, Russian troops entered the company's premises while armed, illegally took up residence there and seized its property. The company lost access to its property complex, movable assets and inventory, as well as the ability to conduct business. The court found the claims justified and ordered the full amount to be recovered from the Russian Federation, represented by the Prosecutor General's Office of the Russian Federation. Agro Alliance LLC was established in 2000. Its founders include Volodymyr Dudka, who also heads the company, Oleh Romanenko and Nina Arshukova. Background: The Commercial Court of Luhansk Oblast previously ordered the Russian Federation to pay Trade House Agrokhim LLC UAH 51.67 million (US$1.1 million) in damages for property lost in Svatove in Luhansk Oblast and Kakhovka in Kherson Oblast. yemen.title: Deadly attack on airport in Saudi Arabia's capital kills 12
yemen.text: Saudi Arabia on Sunday extended the closure of the country's main international airport , according to an online flight tracker, a day after a missile attack on the facility killed 12 people from several countries and left more than 300 injured in a major escalation of the war between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and the kingdom. A Saudi-led coalition blamed Saturday afternoon's attack on the Houthis. It was the latest of several in the past week at King Khalid International Airport in the capital, Riyadh, and marked the deadliest attack in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war. Saudi Arabia is the world's top oil exporter, and the attacks have sent up oil prices and rattled markets. Following the attack, US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was weighing whether the United States would join Saudi strikes against the rebels. Airport operations were suspended Saturday. Authorities later extended the closure until at least 9PM. Sunday, according to Flightradar24. Also on Sunday, the Houthi-run Health Ministry said 91 Yemenis were killed and 168 injured by the Saudi-led coalition in five weeks. It said 60 percent of those killed were women and children. Mix of nationalities killed at Saudi airport The attack struck an airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorised to speak to the media. The Saudi statement said the dead included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said several hospitals were treating the injured. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged in a social media post that an American citizen had been killed in the attack, which he condemned. yemen.title: Attack on Riyadh airport leaves 12 dead, more than 300 injured
yemen.text: Attack on Riyadh airport leaves 12 dead, more than 300 injured At least 12 people were killed and 309 others injured in an attack on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh as Yemen's Houthis escalated the campaign they launched this summer against the kingdom. The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said in a statement on Sunday that four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed in the attack late Saturday. The authority said some of the injured were in critical condition and that all were receiving medical care at several hospitals. Hospitals were flooded with wounded brought by ambulance and helicopter, people briefed on the matter told Reuters. Jordan's foreign ministry said in a statement on Saturday that two injured Jordanians were discharged from hospital while two others were still receiving treatment. yemen.title: Riyadh vows response to airport attack, US weighs involvement
yemen.text: Saudi Arabia on Sunday extended the closure of the country’s main international airport, according to an online flight tracker, a day after a missile attack on the facility killed 12 people from several countries and left more than 300 injured in a major escalation of the war between Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and the kingdom. Following the attack, US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was weighing whether the United States would join Saudi strikes against the rebels. Yemen's Houthis on Sunday renewed their warning to airlines, airport workers, and travellers against using Saudi airports, saying the warning should be taken seriously and that the kingdom "bore responsibility for failed interceptions".

yemen.title: Yemen's Houthis warn against using Saudi airports as Riyadh closure extended
yemen.text: Yemen's Houthis warn against using Saudi airports as Riyadh closure extended Yemen's Houthis on Sunday renewed their warning to airlines, airport workers, and travellers against using Saudi Arabian airports, saying the warning should be taken seriously and that the kingdom "bore responsibility for failed interceptions", after their attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday. The closure of King Khalid International Airport has been extended until 21:00 GMT on Sunday, according to a Notice to Air Missions (Notam) issued by Saudi civil aviation authorities.

yemen.title: Kuwait's Jazeera Airways says Riyadh flights affected by temporary suspension
yemen.text: Kuwait's Jazeera Airways says Riyadh flights affected by temporary suspension Kuwait's Jazeera Airways says its Riyadh flights have been affected by the temporary suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport, where an alleged Houthi strike killed at least 12 people and injured more than 300 others. All flights were diverted from Riyadh on Saturday, and operations at the airport, which serves a city of roughly 8 million people, were temporarily suspended, the Saudi civil aviation authority said.
